atomicity_and_timing.scope: Only confirmed dispatch of the five registered high-risk tools: submit_note_review, review_note, review_document, rebuild_project_index (graph/rag/all) and change_project_member.
atomicity_and_timing.database_guarantee: Business database writes, domain audit rows, tool_execution_keys insertion, consumed pending status and associated session/turn completion share the caller-owned PostgreSQL transaction; nested helpers do not commit it early.
excluded: External embedding/provider requests and charges cannot be rolled back and may repeat when database work fails/retries.
Post-commit confirmation.completed trace event insertion is outside the transaction; trace failure can surface after business commit.
Existing REST file review commits business approval before a separate indexing transaction; its behavior is not covered by the confirmed-tool atomicity claim.
Pool-side permission reads recheck current rights but do not serialize every concurrent revocation throughout the whole transaction.
atomicity_and_timing.external_call_scope: RAG/document indexing holds the confirmation transaction while extracting text/chunking and awaiting embeddings. Default hash embedding is local. openai_compatible invokes HTTP send and response JSON await with no explicit application request timeout in embedding.rs; actual provider cost/time was not measured by these tests.
atomicity_and_timing.lock_scope: Pending action/session locks are held from approval selection until outer commit/rollback. Document sync locks files before dataset/sync rows. Project RAG rebuild locks all approved knowledge-document files in id order before bulk stale updates, then processes all files sequentially in that same transaction. mark_sync_failed updates files before syncs.
atomicity_and_timing.timing_limit: No claim of bounded lock duration or bounded external cost. The 180/1200-second Agent-turn budgets do not wrap the separate approve_pending_action endpoint. SQL initialization's 1-second lock timeout and pool acquisition's 30-second timeout are not an end-to-end confirmation or remote embedding deadline. The regression's 250ms local lock timeout and 5-second observation guard are test settings, not production SLOs. A slow embedding call prolongs already-held DB locks.
